# Subset construction

<!-- Generated by `./scripts/generate-docs.sh`. Do not edit: every step below is a
     sentence the implementation produced while running, and editing them here would make
     this file disagree with the code it documents. -->

Turns an ε-NFA into a DFA. Each state of the DFA stands for the *set* of NFA states the
machine could be in, so the non-determinism is not removed so much as accounted for. The
worklist is the set of subsets discovered but not yet expanded, and the algorithm ends when it
is empty.

## Worked example

Input: `(a|b)*abb`

1. The start state is the ε-closure of {q6} — that is {q0, q2, q4, q6, q7, q8}, which becomes A.
2. Reading `a` from A = {q0, q2, q4, q6, q7, q8} reaches {q0, q1, q2, q4, q5, q7, q8, q9, q10} — that subset is new, so it becomes B and joins the worklist.
3. Reading `b` from A = {q0, q2, q4, q6, q7, q8} reaches {q0, q2, q3, q4, q5, q7, q8} — that subset is new, so it becomes C and joins the worklist.
4. Reading `a` from B = {q0, q1, q2, q4, q5, q7, q8, q9, q10} reaches {q0, q1, q2, q4, q5, q7, q8, q9, q10} — already seen as B, so no new state is created.
5. Reading `b` from B = {q0, q1, q2, q4, q5, q7, q8, q9, q10} reaches {q0, q2, q3, q4, q5, q7, q8, q11, q12} — that subset is new, so it becomes D and joins the worklist.
6. Reading `a` from C = {q0, q2, q3, q4, q5, q7, q8} reaches {q0, q1, q2, q4, q5, q7, q8, q9, q10} — already seen as B, so no new state is created.
7. Reading `b` from C = {q0, q2, q3, q4, q5, q7, q8} reaches {q0, q2, q3, q4, q5, q7, q8} — already seen as C, so no new state is created.
8. Reading `a` from D = {q0, q2, q3, q4, q5, q7, q8, q11, q12} reaches {q0, q1, q2, q4, q5, q7, q8, q9, q10} — already seen as B, so no new state is created.
9. Reading `b` from D = {q0, q2, q3, q4, q5, q7, q8, q11, q12} reaches {q0, q2, q3, q4, q5, q7, q8, q13} — that subset is new, so it becomes E and joins the worklist.
10. Reading `a` from E = {q0, q2, q3, q4, q5, q7, q8, q13} reaches {q0, q1, q2, q4, q5, q7, q8, q9, q10} — already seen as B, so no new state is created.
11. Reading `b` from E = {q0, q2, q3, q4, q5, q7, q8, q13} reaches {q0, q2, q3, q4, q5, q7, q8} — already seen as C, so no new state is created.
12. No subsets left to expand. The DFA has 5 states, 1 of them accepting.

**Result.** a DFA with 5 states, from an ε-NFA with 14.

Every line above is a `Step` returned by the same function the editor calls. The
step-through at [/convert](https://kleene.pranavmshukla.in/convert) renders these sentences,
`kleene --verbose` prints them, and this page is generated from them.
